official_measurement_examples.name: Ancient woodland definition
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England describes ancient woodland as land wooded continuously since at least 1600 and treats it as an irreplaceable habitat.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 inventory precedence
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's 29 April 2026 dataset states that revised Ancient Woodland Inventory data for completed counties takes precedence over the older England dataset; unrevised counties continue to use the older inventory as primary reference.

official_measurement_examples.name: Small woodland inventory limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Standing advice warns that ancient woodlands smaller than 2 hectares may not appear on inventories, while the revised inventory is adding smaller 0.25 to 2 hectare sites county by county.

official_measurement_examples.name: Irreplaceable habitat planning gate
official_measurement_examples.fact: National planning policy says development causing loss or deterioration of ancient woodland or ancient or veteran trees should be refused unless wholly exceptional reasons and a suitable compensation strategy exist.

official_measurement_examples.name: 500 metre consultation scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Forestry Commission guidance describes it as a non-statutory consultee for development affecting or within 500 metres of ancient woodland; that consultation distance is not itself a statutory prohibition zone.

official_measurement_examples.name: Felling licence separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Forestry Commission guidance published 8 July 2026 says most growing-tree felling in England requires a felling licence unless an exemption applies; planning and felling permissions remain distinct regimes.

official_measurement_examples.name: Forestry EIA separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Forestry Commission guidance states woodland projects likely to have significant environmental effects can require stage-2 forestry EIA consent under the forestry EIA regime before work proceeds.

official_measurement_examples.name: BNG irreplaceable habitat distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Defra guidance lists ancient woodland and ancient or veteran trees as irreplaceable habitat; biodiversity-gain treatment must not be represented as ordinary replaceable-habitat offsetting or as parcel development clearance.

core_rules: ancient-woodland inventory evidence is not by itself a complete planning decision
absence from an inventory is not proof ancient woodland is absent
revised completed-county inventory takes precedence where Natural England says it does
older inventory remains primary reference where a county has not yet been revised
planning permission is not a felling licence
a felling licence is not planning permission
forestry EIA consent is not planning permission
a 500 metre Forestry Commission consultation distance is not a statutory development exclusion zone
irreplaceable-habitat compensation is not evidence the lost habitat is replaceable
ancient or veteran tree status does not determine land ownership
wood-pasture or parkland inventory evidence must retain its dataset scope and date
historic inventory geometry must not silently override newer authoritative revisions
tree-felling exemptions must not be assumed without matching the current Forestry Commission rules
planning policy protection does not create access rights or reserve development capacity
no parcel ancient-woodland clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
